content.value_statement: API reviews can miss authorization flaws, unsafe inputs, weak rate limits, and exposed errors. This skill organizes authorized REST and GraphQL testing into seven focused phases.
actual_capabilities: Organizes API discovery, authentication, authorization, input validation, rate limiting, GraphQL, and error handling into seven phases.
Provides test topics for API keys, JWT tokens, OAuth2 flows, token expiration, and refresh tokens.
Covers object, function, role, privilege, and tenant authorization boundaries.
Identifies checks for SQL, NoSQL, command, and XXE injection risks.
Supplies an API security checklist and quality gates for findings, remediation, and reporting.
References companion skills for deeper fuzzing, scanning, authentication, authorization, and security auditing.
limitations: The skill provides a workflow and prompts but does not execute security tests.
Several phases depend on companion skills that may not be installed.
Environment-specific endpoints, roles, credentials, and safety limits must be supplied.
Results require validation by qualified security reviewers before operational decisions.

use_cases.title: Review a New API
use_cases.description: Build a pre-release checklist for authentication, authorization, validation, rate limiting, and error handling.

use_cases.title: Plan a Security Assessment
use_cases.description: Create a phased REST or GraphQL assessment with evidence requirements and quality gates.

use_cases.title: Structure Authorized Research
use_cases.description: Map approved endpoints and test categories before conducting controlled vulnerability research.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a security checklist for my [REST or GraphQL] API. Cover authentication, authorization, input validation, rate limiting, errors, HTTPS, CORS, and logging.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when beginning an authorized API review.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Identity Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan authentication and authorization tests for [API]. Include [roles], token lifecycle, object access, function access, privilege changes, and tenant isolation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when reviewing identity and access controls.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Controlled Test Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a test matrix for [endpoints] within [scope]. Include expected results, safe inputs, rate limits, stop conditions, evidence, and remediation fields.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when preparing a repeatable assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Comprehensive Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Produce a seven-phase REST and GraphQL security plan for [system]. Prioritize risks, map roles and data flows, define controls, and specify quality gates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a complex, authorized API security engagement.

output_examples.input: Create an authorization test plan for a multi-tenant REST API.
output: Scope: Verify object, function, role, and tenant boundaries across documented endpoints.
Method: Compare permitted and denied requests for each role using approved test accounts.
Evidence: Record request context, expected policy, actual result, impact, and remediation.

output_examples.input: Review the test coverage for a GraphQL endpoint.
output: Discovery: Inventory queries, mutations, types, and enabled introspection within the approved schema.
Controls: Check depth, complexity, batching, field suggestions, authentication, authorization, and sanitized errors.
Quality gate: Document confirmed issues, supporting evidence, severity, and practical remediation.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, scope, test accounts, rate limits, and stop conditions before sending requests.
Start with documented endpoints and low-impact checks, then increase test depth only within approved boundaries.
Record reproducible evidence and separate confirmed vulnerabilities from observations that require validation.
anti_patterns: Do not test production systems without explicit authorization and an approved impact plan.
Do not treat generic checklists as proof that an API is secure.
Do not run brute force, resource exhaustion, or injection tests without controlled limits and monitoring.

faq.question: Does this skill run security tools?
faq.answer: No. It provides a structured workflow, checklists, prompts, and references to companion skills.

faq.question: Does it support both REST and GraphQL?
faq.answer: Yes. Shared phases cover REST and GraphQL, with a dedicated phase for GraphQL-specific controls.

faq.question: What access information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide approved endpoints, roles, test accounts, token flows, tenant boundaries, rate limits, and prohibited actions.

faq.question: Can I use it against a production API?
faq.answer: Only with explicit authorization, controlled limits, monitoring, stop conditions, and an approved impact plan.

faq.question: Does the workflow prove an API is secure?
faq.answer: No. It improves coverage, but qualified reviewers must validate results and assess environment-specific risks.

faq.question: Which companion skills are referenced?
faq.answer: It references API fuzzing, scanning, authentication, authorization, injection testing, security auditing, and web security workflows.
